# locker_sync_tool

[← Command index](README.md)

Sync a primary locker to one or more secondary lockers, reviewing each change in an editor.

## Synopsis

```
locker_sync_tool [options]
```

## Description

Treats one locker as authoritative (the primary, `Hetzner` by default) and brings each
secondary locker (`Gdrive,External` by default) into line with it. For each secondary
it:

1. Builds an MD5 hash map of the primary and the secondary. Local lockers are hashed
   on disk; remotes are listed with `rclone lsjson --hash`, falling back to the
   `.locker_hashes.db` sidecar when the remote returns no hashes. SFTP remotes such as
   Hetzner always use the sidecar.
2. Works out the actions: COPY for files only on the primary, UPDATE for files whose
   hash differs, and RECYCLE for orphans that exist only on the secondary.
3. Opens your editor with the actions. COPY and UPDATE lines are active; RECYCLE lines
   are commented out, so orphans are kept unless you uncomment them. Delete or comment
   a line to skip it; delete every line to skip that secondary.
4. Runs the approved actions, one batched transfer per kind of cryption.

Files are decrypted when going from a locker marked `encrypted` to one that is not
(with the primary's passphrase) and encrypted the other way (with the secondary's).
Each secondary's configured `excluded_dirs` are left out of both the comparison and the
writes, and its `.recycle_bin` is never compared.

After a successful sync, when the primary is a local locker and the secondary is an
SFTP remote, the secondary's hash sidecar is refreshed from the local content. For an
unattended, additive local-to-remote backup use `master_backup`.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-l, --primary_locker <primary_locker>` | Authoritative locker that the secondaries are brought in line with. Default: `Hetzner`. Allowed: `All`, `Local`, `Hetzner`, `Gdrive`, `External`. |
| `-s, --secondary_lockers <secondary_lockers>` | Comma-separated locker names to update; unknown names are skipped with a warning. Default: `Gdrive,External`. |
| `--skip_cache` | Rebuild every hash map instead of reusing one cached within the last 24 hours. |
| `--clear_cache` | Delete every cached hash map before starting, not just those of the lockers in this run. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Sync Hetzner to Gdrive and External

```bash
locker_sync_tool
```

### Show the actions without transferring anything

```bash
locker_sync_tool -p -v
```

### Sync the local locker to Gdrive only

```bash
locker_sync_tool -l Local -s Gdrive
```

### Rehash everything instead of using the cached hash maps

```bash
locker_sync_tool --skip_cache -v
```

### Delete all cached hash maps, then sync

```bash
locker_sync_tool --clear_cache
```

## Notes

- Hash maps are cached per locker for 24 hours, including the primary's, so recent changes are not seen until the cache expires unless `--skip_cache` or `--clear_cache` is given. Caches are written even on pretend runs.
- After a sync the secondary's cached map is updated with the files just transferred, so a re-run within the cache window does not transfer them again.
- Recycled orphans go to the secondary's `.recycle_bin`; nothing is hard-deleted.
- For SFTP remotes the comparison is only as accurate as the sidecar. Keep it current with `master_backup` or `rebuild_hash_sidecars`.
- There is no preview prompt, so `--no-preview` has no effect; the editor is the review step.
